arxiv-1803-04323.title: The formation of astrophysical Mg-rich silicate dust
arxiv-1803-04323.creator: Christopher M. Mauney, Davide Lazzati
arxiv-1803-04323.description: Abstract We present new results for ground-state candidate energies of Mg-rich olivine (MRO) clusters and use the binding energies of these clusters to determine their nucleation rates in stellar outflows, with particular interest in the environments of core-collapse supernovae (CCSNe).

arxiv-2103-12874.title: Using Meta-learning to Recommend Process Discovery Methods Thanks: The authors would like to thank CNPq (National Council for the Scientific and Technological Development) for their financial support under Grant of Project 420562/2018-4 and 309863/2020-1 and the program “Piano di sostegno alla ricer
arxiv-2103-12874.creator: Sylvio Barbon Junior, Paolo Ceravolo, Ernesto Damiani, Gabriel Marques Tavares
arxiv-2103-12874.description: Abstract Process discovery methods have obtained remarkable achievements in Process Mining, delivering comprehensible process models to enhance management capabilities. However, selecting the suitable method for a specific event log highly relies on human expertise, hindering its broad application. Solutions based on Meta-learning (MtL) have been promising for creating systems with reduced human assistance.

arxiv-2210-06090.title: Can We “Sense” the Call of The Ocean? Current Advances in Remote Sensing Computational Imaging for Marine Debris Monitoring Journal: Elsevier
arxiv-2210-06090.creator: Oktay Karakuş
arxiv-2210-06090.description: Abstract Especially due to the unconscious use of petroleum products, the ocean faces a potential danger: plastic pollution . Plastic pollutes not only the ocean but also directly the air and foods whilst endangering the ocean wild-life due to the ingestion and entanglements.

arxiv-2301-07573.title: Synthcity: facilitating innovative use cases of synthetic data in different data modalities
arxiv-2301-07573.creator: Zhoazhi Qian zhaozhi.qian@maths.cam.ac.uk, Bogdan-Constantin Cebere bcc38@cam.ac.uk, Mihaela van der Schaar mv472@cam.ac.uk
arxiv-2301-07573.description: Abstract Synthcity is an open-source software package for innovative use cases of synthetic data in ML fairness, privacy and augmentation across diverse tabular data modalities, including static data, regular and irregular time series, data with censoring, multi-source data, composite data, and more. Synthcity provides the practitioners with a single access point to cutting edge research and tools in synthetic data.

arxiv-2307-03896.title: On a cylindrical scanning modality in three-dimensional Compton scatter tomography \ddmmyyyydate August 9, 2026 \currenttime
arxiv-2307-03896.creator: James W. Webber † \dagger
arxiv-2307-03896.description: Abstract . We present injectivity and microlocal analyses of a new generalized Radon transform, ℛ \mathcal{R} , which has applications to a novel scanner design in three-dimensional Compton Scattering Tomography (CST), which we also introduce here. Using Fourier decomposition and Volterra equation theory, we prove that ℛ \mathcal{R} is injective and show that the image solution is unique.

arxiv-2311-06366.title: Higher-dimensional Holographic Superconductors in Born-Infeld Electrodynamics and f ⁡ ( R ) f(R) Gravity
arxiv-2311-06366.creator: Alexandar Roussev
arxiv-2311-06366.description: Abstract In this paper, the properties of higher dimensional holographic superconductors are studied in the background of f ⁡ ( R ) f(R) gravity and Born-Infeld electrodynamics. A specific model of f ⁡ ( R ) f(R) gravity is considered, allowing a perturbative approach to the problem.

arxiv-2405-08401.title: Realtime Global Optimization of a Fail-Safe Emergency Stop Maneuver for Arbitrary Electrical / Electronical Failures in Automated Driving*
arxiv-2405-08401.creator: F. Duerr, J. Ziehn, R. Kohlhaas, M. Roschani, M. Ruf, J. Beyerer
arxiv-2405-08401.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by F. Duerr, J. Ziehn, R. Kohlhaas, M. Roschani, M. Ruf, J. Beyerer. In the event of a critical system failures in automated vehicles, fail-operational or fail-safe measures provide minimum guarantees for the vehicle’s performance, depending on which of its subsystems remain operational. Various such methods have been proposed which, upon failure, use different remaining sets of operational subsystems to execute maneuvers that bring the vehicle into a safe state under different environmental conditions.

arxiv-2409-12082.title: ReLU Surrogates in Mixed-Integer MPC for Irrigation Scheduling
arxiv-2409-12082.creator: Bernard T. Agyeman, Jinfeng Liu, Sirish L. Shah
arxiv-2409-12082.description: Abstract Efficient water management in agriculture is important for mitigating the growing freshwater scarcity crisis. Mixed-integer Model Predictive Control (MPC) has emerged as an effective approach for addressing the complex scheduling problems in agricultural irrigation. However, the computational complexity of mixed-integer MPC still poses a significant challenge, particularly in large-scale applications.

arxiv-2411-17572.title: Log-concavity of polynomials arising from equivariant cohomology Thanks: Jacob Matherne received support from a Simons Foundation Travel Support for Mathematicians Award MPS-TSM-00007970.
arxiv-2411-17572.creator: Yairon Cid-Ruiz, Yupeng Li, Jacob P. Matherne
arxiv-2411-17572.description: Abstract . We study the equivariant cohomology classes of torus-equivariant subvarieties of the space of matrices. For a large class of torus actions, we prove that the polynomials representing these classes (up to suitably changing signs) are covolume polynomials in the sense of Aluffi.

arxiv-2502-15045.title: Quantum thermodynamic advantage in work extraction from steerable quantum correlations
arxiv-2502-15045.creator: Tanmoy Biswas, Chandan Datta, Luis Pedro García-Pintos
arxiv-2502-15045.description: Abstract Inspired by the primary goal of quantum thermodynamics—to characterize quantum signatures and leverage their benefits in thermodynamic scenarios—, we design a work extraction task within a bipartite framework that exhibits a quantum thermodynamic advantage. The steerability of quantum correlations between the two parties is the key resource enabling such an advantage.

arxiv-2506-23211.title: Some invariant connections on symplectic reductive homogeneous spaces August 8, 2026 Journal: ⋯ \cdots
arxiv-2506-23211.creator: Abdelhak Abouqateb, Othmane Dani
arxiv-2506-23211.description: Abstract A symplectic reductive homogeneous space is a pair ( G / H , Ω ) (G/H,\Omega) , where G / H G/H is a reductive homogeneous G G -space and Ω \Omega is a G G -invariant symplectic form on it. The main examples include symplectic Lie groups, symplectic symmetric spaces, and flag manifolds.

arxiv-2510-25199.title: AI-Powered Early Detection of Critical Diseases using Image Processing and Audio Analysis
arxiv-2510-25199.creator: Manisha More, Kavya Bhand, Kaustubh Mukdam, Kavya Sharma, Manas Kawtikwar, Prajwal Kavhar, Hridayansh Kaware
arxiv-2510-25199.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Manisha More, Kavya Bhand, Kaustubh Mukdam, Kavya Sharma, Manas Kawtikwar, Prajwal Kavhar, Hridayansh Kaware. Early diagnosis of critical diseases can significantly improve patient survival and reduce treatment costs. However, existing diagnostic techniques are often costly, invasive, and inaccessible in low-resource regions. This paper presents a multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) diagnostic framework integrating image analysis, thermal imaging, and audio signal processing for early detection of three major health conditions: skin cancer, vascular blood clots, and cardiopulmonary abnormalities.

pmc-10571537.title: The Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic on Cancer Mortality in Pennsylvania: A Retrospective Study with Geospatial Analysis
pmc-10571537.creator: Savanna G Ledford, Fritz Kessler, Jennifer L Moss, Ming Wang, Eugene J Lengerich, Mark Gorrell
pmc-10571537.description: Simple SummaryThe COVID-19 pandemic may have impacted cancer mortality rates by disrupting patient health behaviors and access to cancer care, as well as being directly affected by infection with SARS-CoV-2. There is limited population-based research that investigates the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on cancer mortality in the United States.

pmc-11437616.title: Analysis of the structure of Basic Health Units in Brazil to conduct telehealth actions: a comparison of two cross-sectional studies
pmc-11437616.creator: Denise Oliveira Franco, Mauro Henrique Nogueira Guimarães Abreu, Rafaela Silveira Pinto, Antônio Thomaz Gonzaga Matta-Machado, Renata Castro Martins
pmc-11437616.description: BackgroundTelehealth uses Information and Communication Technologies (ICT) in distance health-related activities between professionals, managers, and patients of health services. This cross-sectional study compared the ICT infrastructure available in Brazilian Basic Health Units (BHU) for telehealth actions, along with evaluation cycles of the National Program for Improving Access and Quality of Primary Care (PMAQ-AB).

pmc-11503876.title: Effects of Different Photoperiods on Growth Performance, Glucose Metabolism, Acetylcholine, and Its Relative Acetylcholine Receptor Modulation in Broiler Chickens
pmc-11503876.creator: Miao Yu, Mengjie Xu, Guangju Wang, Jinghai Feng, Minhong Zhang, Alessandro Dal Bosco
pmc-11503876.description: Simple SummaryLong photoperiods are commonly used in modern intensive broiler chicken farming, which are crucial environmental factors in the growth and health of broilers. Through different photoperiods experiments, we found that extending the photoperiods could promote the growth rate of broilers while reducing the feed efficiency, inhibiting acetylcholine and its relative-acetylcholine receptor expression, and inducing glucose metabolism disorders in broilers.

pmc-11692170.title: FRAILTY TRAJECTORIES AND ITS ASSOCIATED FACTORS IN JAPANESE OLDER ADULTS
pmc-11692170.creator: Yu Taniguchi, Akihiko Kitamura, Toshiki Hata, Koji Fujita, Takumi Abe, Yu Nofuji, Satoshi Seino, Yuri Yokoyama
pmc-11692170.description: The present study had two objectives: to identify aging trajectories in frailty status from age 65–90 years among community-dwelling older Japanese; and to identify factors associated with this trajectory among these people. The present prospective study used repeated measures data on frailty status from a 13-year longitudinal study.

pmc-13079371.title: Effect of early physical therapy initiation and adherence on functional outcomes after arthroscopic rotator cuff repair: a prospective observational cohort study
pmc-13079371.creator: Abdullah Raizah, Ravi Shankar Reddy, Mastour Saeed Alshahrani, Faisal M. Alyazedi, Batool Abdulelah Alkhamis, Saleh Kardm, Ghada Mohamed Koura, Devika Rani Sangadala, Debjani Mukherjee
pmc-13079371.description: IntroductionRotator cuff repair outcomes are influenced not only by surgical technique but also by postoperative rehabilitation. However, the optimal timing of physical therapy (PT) initiation and the role of adherence remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to evaluate the independent and combined effects of early PT initiation and adherence on functional recovery following arthroscopic rotator cuff repair.

pmc-13675456.title: Microbial cell factories for gamma-linolenic acid biosynthesis: metabolic engineering, downstream processing, and future perspectives
pmc-13675456.creator: Jie Qiao, Wei Wang, Peiyao Duan, Zhili Zhang, Rongrong Yang, Haiyang Cui, Xiujuan Li
pmc-13675456.description: Gamma-linolenic acid (GLA) is a vital anti-inflammatory polyunsaturated fatty acid, yet its traditional supply from plant seeds such as evening primrose and borage is constrained by low yields and climatic instability. Consequently, microbial cell factories present a sustainable and season-independent alternative for scalable GLA production. This review critically synthesizes recent biotechnological advancements in utilizing oleaginous microorganisms as production platforms.

pmc-13700051.title: Revisiting Globalized CAD Risk Assessment in the Era of Artificial Intelligence
pmc-13700051.creator: Junjie Yang, Ran Xin
pmc-13700051.description: Corresponding Author Coronary artery disease (CAD) remains the leading cause of mortality worldwide.1 Studies have consistently documented a disproportionately increased burden of obstructive CAD among specific Asian ethnic subgroups, particularly those of South Asian ancestry.2 The pretest probability (PTP) assessment for CAD serves as a foundation for clinical decision-making, directly influencing diagnostic pathways, resource allocation, and ultimately patient outcomes.
